title.value: Dynamic Kinetic Asymmetric Allylic Alkylations of Allenes

abstract.value: Efficient and atom economic<sup>1</sup> methods for construction of chiral allenes are of significance due to the presence of this core structure in numerous natural and biologically important products,<sup>2</sup> as well as synthetic intermediates for asymmetric synthesis of targets involving chirality transfer.<sup>2,3</sup> Undoubtedly, the potential in this latter regard has been retarded by the limited accessibility of enantioenriched allenes. Typically, chiral allenes are derived from chiral propargylic alcohols.<sup>2,4</sup> Only recently has asymmetric catalysis been employed for the construction of allenes.<sup>2,5</sup> Several limited methods utilize the asymmetric addition of soft nucleophiles to vinyl allyl Pd(II) intermediates accessed through both the oxidative addition of racemic 2,3-alkadienyl phosphates<sup>6</sup> and prochiral vinyl bromides.<sup>7</sup> Our group has been active in related palladium-catalyzed asymmetric allylic alkylations (AAA) through a dynamic kinetic asymmetric transformation (DYKAT) utilizing our ligands.<sup>8</sup> Therefore, we focused our studies on the use of these ligands for the dynamic kinetic asymmetric addition of nucleophiles to allenes (eq 1), which has led to a general access to allenes of high enantiomeric excess for both carbon- and nitrogen-based nucleophiles. Further, a most unusual dependence of enantioselectivity on base in the case of amine nucleophiles has been uncovered.
